description: §14.8.9 declassification is VALUE-scoped — a `reveal("passwordHash")` applied to a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT query's row (`WHERE id = 999`) does not silence the raw-egress gate for the row actually returned (`WHERE id = ${id}`), which was never revealed. E-PROTECT-004 fires. Pins the fix for the third measured fail-open: the deleted suppressor was a body-wide lexeme test (`/\.\s*reveal\s*\(/` over the function's source slice), so ANY reveal anywhere in the body disarmed the gate for every value in it.
rationale: §14.8.9 scopes declassification to the value: reveal is applied 'at the value' (SPEC.md:8506-8507), it 'stamps the named column's provenance descriptor as declassified-at-this-value', and 'the serializer admits a protected-origin column only when its descriptor bears a `reveal` stamp at the sink' (SPEC.md:8511-8513); the worked example is commented 'here only' (SPEC.md:8509). A body-wide suppressor violates every one of those four phrases at once — the returned row `u` bears no stamp, and the stamped value `decoy` is not the one that crosses the wire. This is the shape that makes the defect a security bug rather than an ergonomic one: an inserted reveal launders every sibling value in the function for free. provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S352 (dpa-033 (c)).
